title: Deconstructing Stage-Wise Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems: Drift Isolation, Adversarial Limits, and Pre-Registered Benchmarks (code, results and pre-registrations)
description: Code, result files, label corrections and pre-registration texts for the paper "Deconstructing Stage-Wise Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems: Drift Isolation, Adversarial Limits, and Pre-Registered Benchmarks". The paper asks whether splitting a plant into its physical stages, with one detector per stage (PIVOT), catches attacks better than one detector for the whole plant, and tests this under strict rules: thresholds come from normal data only, every count of attacks caught is compared with what the same alarms would catch by chance, and eight hypotheses were written down before they were tested on unused data (further HAI releases, and SWaT releases recorded years after the training data). Three of 20 release-level verdicts supported the hypotheses. The repository contains the evaluation code, the result files the paper's numbers are computed from, the record of an independent re-run, label corrections for HAI 23.05, WADI and SWaT July 2019, and the hypothesis texts H1-H6 with their outcomes. The folder legacy_preliminary/ holds the earlier investigation ("Physics-Informed Voting Over Subsystems") that the paper refers to; its results are superseded by the paper. The SWaT, WADI and HAI datasets are not included and must be obtained from their maintainers. Published for academic reproducibility only; all rights reserved (see LICENSE).
